from manim import *
import numpy as np
import random

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title_text = "The Digital Treasure Chest"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Meet Cipher, guarding a chest with 256 switches.",
            "- A cryptographic hash is like a digital fingerprint.",
            "- Every bit must match to unlock the treasure.",
            "- Guessing one bit wrong keeps the chest shut.",
            "- How hard is it to guess all 256?"
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_CIPHER = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_CHEST = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_BIT = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_LOCKED = "#FF0000"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Meet Cipher, guarding a chest with 256 switches.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Cipher the Dragon: Stylized triangle
        dragon = Triangle(color=COLOR_CIPHER, fill_opacity=0.8).rotate(-90*DEGREES)
        dragon_label = Text("Cipher", font_size=16, color=COLOR_CIPHER).next_to(dragon, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        cipher_group = VGroup(dragon, dragon_label)
        self.place_at_grid(cipher_group, 'D2', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Treasure Chest
        chest_box = Rectangle(width=1.0, height=0.7, color=COLOR_CHEST, fill_opacity=0.5)
        chest_lock = Dot(color=COLOR_CHEST).move_to(chest_box.get_center())
        chest_group = VGroup(chest_box, chest_lock)
        self.place_at_grid(chest_group, 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(cipher_group), Create(chest_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # A cryptographic hash is like a digital fingerprint.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Fingerprint: Concentric Arcs
        fingerprint = VGroup(*[Arc(radius=0.1*i, start_angle=0, angle=PI*1.4, color=WHITE) for i in range(1, 5)])
        self.place_at_grid(fingerprint, 'B3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(fingerprint))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Every bit must match to unlock the treasure.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # 256 slots: 16x16 grid of small squares
        slots = VGroup()
        for i in range(16):
            for j in range(16):
                slot = Square(side_length=0.05, color=WHITE, stroke_width=1)
                slots.add(slot)
        
        slots.arrange_in_grid(rows=16, cols=16, buff=0.03)
        # Using A1 to C6 to define the area for the bits
        self.place_in_area(slots, 'A1', 'C6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(slots), FadeOut(fingerprint))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Guessing one bit wrong keeps the chest shut.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Random bits flashing to represent guessing
        flash_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def flash_slots_updater(mobject):
            # Use tracker value to vary the seed
            seed_val = int(flash_tracker.get_value() * 100)
            rng = random.Random(seed_val)
            for _ in range(40):
                idx = rng.randint(0, 255)
                # Toggle fill opacity
                mobject[idx].set_fill(WHITE, opacity=rng.random())

        slots.add_updater(flash_slots_updater)
        self.play(flash_tracker.animate.set_value(10), run_time=2)
        slots.remove_updater(flash_slots_updater)
        
        # Stop and show one failure
        for s in slots:
            s.set_fill(WHITE, opacity=0.8)
            
        bad_bit_idx = 100 # Arbitrary bit to fail
        self.play(
            slots[bad_bit_idx].animate.set_color(COLOR_LOCKED).set_fill(COLOR_LOCKED, opacity=1.0),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        # 'Locked' icon/label
        locked_text = Text("LOCKED", font_size=24, color=COLOR_LOCKED, weight=BOLD)
        self.place_at_grid(locked_text, 'D5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(locked_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # How hard is it to guess all 256?
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Dragon breathes a small green flame
        flame_particles = VGroup(*[
            Triangle(color=COLOR_CIPHER, fill_opacity=0.8).scale(0.05) 
            for _ in range(8)
        ])
        
        # Initial positions at dragon's snout
        snout_pos = dragon.get_right()
        for p in flame_particles:
            p.move_to(snout_pos)
            
        def flame_updater(mobject, dt):
            for i, p in enumerate(mobject):
                # Particles move right at slightly different speeds
                speed = 2.5 + (i % 3) * 0.4
                p.shift(RIGHT * speed * dt)
                # Reset if they hit the chest area
                if p.get_x() > chest_group.get_x():
                    p.move_to(snout_pos)

        self.add(flame_particles)
        flame_particles.add_updater(flame_updater)
        self.wait(3)
        flame_particles.remove_updater(flame_updater)

        self.wait(2)

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

    def construct(self):
        # Topic: Visualizing the Number: 2^256
        lecture_lines = [
            "2 to the 256 is an unfathomable number.",
            "Imagine every grain of sand on all Earth's beaches.",
            "Now, think of every atom in our entire galaxy.",
            "This number is nearly atoms in the observable universe.",
            "It is a mathematical fortress of impossible scale."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Number: 2^256", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        SAND_COLOR = "#C2B280"
        GOLD_COLOR = "#FFD700"
        GREY_COLOR = "#D3D3D3"
        GALAXY_COLOR = "#1E90FF"

        # Assets
        SAND_ASSET = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sand.svg"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Line: 2 to the 256 is an unfathomable number.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GOLD_COLOR)
        
        # A single grain of sand [Asset: sand.svg] (#C2B280) highlighted
        grain = SVGMobject(SAND_ASSET).set_color(SAND_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(grain, "C3", "D4", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # Glowing effect around the grain
        glow = Arc(radius=0.3, angle=TAU, color=WHITE).set_stroke(opacity=0.4, width=2)
        glow.move_to(grain)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(grain), Create(glow), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Line: Imagine every grain of sand on all Earth's beaches.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(SAND_COLOR)
        
        # Rapid zoom out to sphere of all sand (optimized dot count)
        sand_sphere = Circle(radius=1.8, color=SAND_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.2).set_stroke(width=1)
        np.random.seed(42)
        sand_dots = VGroup(*[
            Dot(
                point=[np.random.uniform(-1.6, 1.6), np.random.uniform(-1.6, 1.6), 0],
                radius=0.015,
                color=SAND_COLOR,
                fill_opacity=np.random.uniform(0.4, 0.7)
            ) for _ in range(80) # Reduced count for performance
        ])
        
        # Keep dots inside circle
        for dot in sand_dots:
            if np.linalg.norm(dot.get_center()) > 1.6:
                dot.set_opacity(0)
        
        sand_visual = VGroup(sand_sphere, sand_dots)
        self.place_in_area(sand_visual, "B2", "E5")
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(glow),
            ReplacementTransform(grain, sand_visual),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=smooth
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line: Now, think of every atom in our entire galaxy.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GALAXY_COLOR)
        
        # Transform into a swirling galaxy (optimized star count)
        galaxy = VGroup()
        num_arms = 3
        stars_per_arm = 30
        for i in range(num_arms):
            start_angle = i * (TAU / num_arms)
            for j in range(stars_per_arm):
                r = (j / stars_per_arm) * 1.7 + 0.2
                theta = r * 3.0 + start_angle
                star = Dot(
                    point=[r * np.cos(theta), r * np.sin(theta), 0],
                    radius=0.012,
                    color=WHITE,
                    fill_opacity=np.random.uniform(0.5, 1.0)
                )
                galaxy.add(star)
        
        galaxy_center = Dot(radius=0.1, color=WHITE).set_style(fill_opacity=0.8)
        galaxy.add(galaxy_center)
        self.place_in_area(galaxy, "B2", "E5")
        
        # Use ValueTracker for rotation to avoid expensive updaters if possible, 
        # but the prompt prefers updaters. Let's use a very simple one.
        galaxy.add_updater(lambda m, dt: m.rotate(0.1 * dt))

        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(sand_visual, galaxy),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Line: This number is nearly atoms in the observable universe.

        self.lecture[3].set_color(GREY_COLOR)

        self.lecture[4].set_color(GOLD_COLOR)

            galaxy.animate.scale(0.8),
            run_time=2

            "Even billions of supercomputers would take trillions of years.",
            "Time itself is too short to crack this code."

        bot_label.next_to(turbo_bot, UP, buff=0.1)

        # Counter
        counter_val = ValueTracker(0)
        counter_text = Text("Keys Checked:", font_size=14, color=WHITE)
        counter_num = DecimalNumber(0, num_decimal_places=0, group_with_commas=True, font_size=18, color=COUNTER_COLOR)
        counter_num.add_updater(lambda d: d.set_value(counter_val.get_value()))
        
        counter_group = VGroup(counter_text, counter_num).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(counter_group, "C3")

        self.play(FadeIn(turbo_bot), FadeIn(bot_label), FadeIn(counter_group))
        self.play(counter_val.animate.set_value(10**12), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)

        # Fill the screen with tiny bots
        # Area A1 to D6
        bots_grid = VGroup()
        for r in ["A", "B", "C", "D"]:
            for c in ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]:
                if r == "B" and c == "3": continue # Skip the main bot area

outline.topic: The Impregnable Fortress: Understanding 256-bit Hash Security
outline.target_audience: High school students and introductory computer science enthusiasts

sections.title: The Digital Treasure Chest
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a cryptographic hash as a 'digital fingerprint' or a lock that can only be opened by one specific key. Establish the mission: How hard is it to guess a 256-bit key?
sections.example: A digital dragon named 'Cipher' guards a chest. To open it, you must guess a sequence of 256 ones and zeros. If you get even one digit wrong, the lock stays shut.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Power of Doubling
sections.content: Explain binary combinations. Each bit added doubles the number of possibilities. Use a visual grid to show how complexity grows exponentially, not linearly.
sections.example: Visualizing a light switch: 1 switch = 2 paths. 2 switches = 4 paths. 10 switches = 1,024 paths. Now, imagine a wall of 256 switches.

sections.title: Visualizing the Number: 2^256
sections.content: Present the mathematical scale of 2^256 (approximately 1.15 x 10^77). Compare this number to physical entities in the universe to make the abstract magnitude tangible.
sections.example: A zoom-out animation: From a single grain of sand, to all the sand on Earth, to the number of atoms in the Milky Way galaxy. 2^256 is nearly as large as the number of atoms in the observable universe (~10^80).

sections.title: The Brute Force Sisyphus
sections.content: Define 'Brute Force'—trying every possible combination. Calculate the time required to crack the hash using the world's fastest supercomputers.
sections.example: A character named 'Turbo Bot' can check 1 trillion keys per second. Even with 4 billion Turbo Bots working together, it would take trillions of times the current age of the universe to exhaust the search space.

sections.title: Energy vs. Probability
sections.content: Introduce the physical limit of computation. Explain that even if we used the entire energy output of the Sun to power a computer, it wouldn't be enough to cycle through all 256-bit combinations.
sections.example: An infographic showing the Sun's energy being captured by a Dyson Sphere. Even with this 'Infinite Battery,' the laws of thermodynamics suggest the computer would melt before finding the key.

sections.title: Conclusion: Security in Scale
sections.content: Summarize why 256-bit hashes (like SHA-256) are the gold standard for Bitcoin and modern banking. Reiterate that the security comes from the sheer 'mathematical vastness' of the search space.
sections.example: The camera zooms back from the universe into a simple smartphone screen, showing a banking app icon. The message: 'Your data is safe because the math is bigger than the universe.'
